Subject: Final: RFI responses — TAM coverage, escalation paths & incident communications

Hi Olivia (and procurement team),

Thanks again for the questions and patience. Attached is our consolidated RFI response (PDF) and a shared Drive link to editable source material. Below is a concise summary of the key items you asked about — pulled from the full document.

1) TAM coverage model
- Named TAM: included for Enterprise plans with > $250k ARR commitment — primary contact during onboarding and quarterly reviews. Named TAM hours: Mon-Fri 8am–6pm PT (US PST) with on-call escalation tier.
- Pooled TAM: available for smaller commitments; remote coverage Mon-Fri 8am–6pm local region; can escalate to named TAM during go-live windows.
- Onsite days: Standard Enterprise includes up to 4 onsite days during onboarding; additional onsite days available as add-on at pre-negotiated rates.

2) Support hours & SLAs
- Standard support (included): Mon-Fri 8am–6pm local region; ticket triage within 2 business hours; response per severity below.
- 24x7 Sev1 coverage (optional add-on): 1-hour initial response and active pager until mitigation.
- SLA targets (acknowledgement -> initial response):
  • Severity 1 (system down / production-blocking): 1 hour (24x7 add-on) / 4 hours (business-hours only)
  • Severity 2 (major functionality impacted): 4 hours / 8 hours
  • Severity 3 (minor impact / questions): 1 business day

3) Escalation path (high level)
- Tier 0: Automated alerts -> support portal ticket creation
- Tier 1: Support engineer triage (repairs, logs, quick remediation)
- Tier 2: Senior engineer / platform specialist (model/runtime tracing, deep diagnostics)
- Tier 3: Named TAM / Solutions lead -> coordinates cross-functional incident response, customer comms, and executive escalation.

Primary escalation contacts (examples):
- Support Portal: https://support.redwood.ai/ (ticket + chat)
- On-call Pager (Sev1): +1-855-REDFWD-1 (routed to on-call engine)
- Named TAM (when assigned): direct email + cell (privacy-protected until assignment)

4) Incident communications cadence & templates
- Initial notification: within SLA initial response window — includes severity, scope, initial mitigation steps, assigned engineer/TAM, and expected update cadence.
- Status updates: every 60 minutes for Sev1 until mitigation; every 4 hours for Sev2; daily for Sev3 until resolved.
- Post-incident report (PIR): delivered within 72 hours for Sev1; includes root cause analysis, timeline, remedial actions, and repeated occurrence mitigations.

Sample initial notification (sent to stakeholders):
---
Subject: Incident [INC-20260710-42] — Sev1 — Model inference failure impacting checkout API
Time detected: 2026-07-10T06:14:00Z
Impact: 35% reduction in successful inference calls for region-us-west
Assigned: Support Engineer: Anika Rao; TAM: (if assigned)
Immediate action: Rolling restart of inference fleet for impacted pool; toggled fallback to smaller-quantized model for degraded throughput.
Next update: 1 hour
---

5) Audit logs & evidence
- Access: Customers can download support logs and incident traces from the support portal; standard retention 90 days.
- Enterprise add-on: 365-day retention + S3 export + daily export job (48-hour SLA to provision).
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we can provide redacted incident traces on request.

6) Mutual action plan (summary) — Go-live checkpoints
- Week -4: Kickoff with TAM, review runbook and rollback plan
- Week -2: Pre-prod load test & model validation with Redwood support engineers
- Week 0: Go-live day — TAM onsite/remote support, heightened monitoring, 30/60/120 minute check-ins
- Week +2 and +6: Post-launch health review and optimization session

Attachments:
- RFI_AcmeCloud_Support_Response_20260710.pdf (full answers, escalation matrix, templates)
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDefRfiResponses
